inputs.spec_clause_ref: kerml clause 8.2.5.10 (FeatureValuesConcreteSyntax.md, region_sha256 1c63fee57931a524) | sysml clause 8.2.2.6.2 (Usages.md, region_sha256 a6f6e20afeed05e4)
inputs.xtext_rule_text:
FeatureValue returns SysML::FeatureValue :
	( '=' 
	| isInitial ?= ':='
	| isDefault ?= 'default' ( '=' | isInitial ?= ':=' )?
	)
	ownedRelatedElement += OwnedExpression
;

decision: As KerML 8.2.5.10 and SysML 8.2.2.6.2 both state it, in the same words, so one shared unit. One of three introducers comes first, then an OwnedExpression. The introducers are `=` for a bound value, `:=` for an initial value, and `default` for a default, which may itself be followed by `=` or `:=`. The `{ isInitial }` and `{ isDefault }` assignments set properties and consume no tokens. A bare `default` followed directly by the expression is allowed; the clause makes the operator after it optional. The Xtext rule is the same.

evidence.note: FeatureValue = ( '=' | isInitial ?= ':=' | isDefault ?= 'default' ( '=' | isInitial ?= ':=' )? ) ownedRelatedElement += OwnedExpression
line 558: `attribute redefines cargoMass default 0 [kg];`, a bare `default` with no operator after it
line 14: `feature fuelCapacity: Real = sum(tanks.capacity);`, the `=` alternative
line 26: `var feature isPainted : Boolean [1] := false;`, the `:=` alternative
FeatureValue: ( '=' | isInitial ?= ':=' | isDefault ?= 'default' ( '=' | isInitial ?= ':=' )? ) ownedRelatedElement += OwnedExpression. Agrees.
